To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The effect of breathing on the dose to lung cancer patients treated with pencil beam scanned proton therapy is dependent on the patient’s breathing pattern.
the reproducibility of the patient's breath-hold (BH) is an important factor in determining the accuracy of the proton treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of breath-hold reproducibility on the dose to the lung, heart and esophagus for patients with locally-advanced lung cancer (LALC) treated with pencil beam scanned proton therapy.
the effects of breath-hold reproducibility on the dose distributions and the dose-volume parameters of lung tumors treated with proton therapy.
the effect of the breath hold reproducibility on the proton dose distribution for the treatment of a locally-advanced lung cancer with pencil beam scanning (PBS) proton therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of proton beam therapy is not justified for the treatment of early stage lung cancer.
the use of proton pencil beam scanning for lung SBRT is safe and effective.
the use of a proton pencil beam scanning (PBS) system is not a significant factor in the overall outcome for the treatment of locally-advanced lung cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reproducibility of breath-holding has a significant effect on the dose distribution for patients treated with Pencil Beam Scan (PBS) proton therapy for locally-advanced lung cancer.
the effect of the BH reproducibility on the PBT dose distributions is not significant for most patients.

we have demonstrated the feasibility of implementing an in-house, automated, 4DCT simulation system that can generate a 4DCT dataset for a patient from a 3DCT dataset and an external respiratory signal (ERS) in a clinically-acceptable amount of time (less than 10 minutes).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of breath-hold reproducibility is more pronounced for PBT than IMRT.
the reproducibility of a breath hold can significantly affect dose distribution and dose-volume histograms for patients undergoing pencil-beam scanned proton therapy.
the breath-hold reproducibility is an important factor when using proton pencil beam scanning for lung tumors.
